This is a gross allocation measure for the two names, not a predicted 50% portfolio loss and not a measurement of their precise currency sensitivity.

If EGP weakens against USD or USD input costs rise, both businesses could face input-cost and working-capital pressure while revenues remain denominated in EGP. That is a plausible shared economic channel from the supplied exposure descriptions. It makes the two names less diversifying against that particular shock than their separate labels might suggest. Missing return histories do not imply zero correlation, while the qualitative common channel does not justify assigning correlation of one or any other coefficient. Covariance requires paired returns, an observation horizon and variability estimation; adding portfolio values supplies none of these. There is no statistical covariance or calibrated stress-loss estimate here.

Bounded decision: flag the EGP50,000 shared-factor allocation, request hedging and pass-through evidence, and evaluate explicitly labeled common-factor stresses before increasing this exposure. Consider diversification into independently evidenced economic drivers, but do not claim an alternative is uncorrelated without data. These are authored exposures, not real holdings or market observations, and no issuer-specific valuation or trade clearance follows.
